title: A Natural Place in the City
questionPrompt:
Part 2: Describe a natural place in your city that you enjoy visiting.
You should say:
Where the place is
When and why you went there
What the place was like
How you felt about the place

questions.question: Why do people have very different feelings about the same place?
questions.sampleAnswer: People experience urban spaces through distinct emotional filters and sensory sensitivities. An introverted reader might perceive a secluded riverbank as a restorative sanctuary, whereas someone seeking dynamic social interaction might find that same quietude desolate or uninspiring.

questions.question: How have public places changed in recent years?
questions.sampleAnswer: Public spaces have progressively shifted from utilitarian paved plazas toward multi-functional ecological corridors. Modern developments integrate permeable landscaping, ambient solar-powered lighting, and pedestrianized greenbelts rather than sterile concrete walkways.

questions.question: What can cities do to make places more pleasant for residents?
questions.sampleAnswer: Municipalities should prioritize biophilic architecture and accessible neighborhood pocket parks. Restricting vehicular congestion adjacent to civic greenspaces and incorporating shaded seating significantly enhances community well-being and daily livability.

cueCardPoints: When and why you went there
How you felt about the place
sampleAnswer:
I'd like to describe a natural place in my city that I love to visit — a riverside park near the centre. It is a long green strip along the river, with towering trees, colourful flower beds, and a walking and cycling path that runs for several kilometres. Even in the middle of the city, it feels surprisingly tranquil and leafy.
I usually go there in the early morning or at sunset, when it is peaceful and uncrowded, sometimes with my parents and sometimes on my own. I love the fresh, clean air and the quiet — you can hear the birds and the water instead of traffic. I often walk for about an hour along the shady, spacious paths, and I always feel calmer and more relaxed afterwards.
What makes it special to me is that it is a peaceful escape from the busy city, so I have made it a habit to go there whenever I feel stressed. I really enjoy this place, and I would recommend it to anyone who needs a break from city life.
